candidates.proposed_modification: Replace the implant-abutment connection with a Morse taper (conical) connection.
candidates.mechanistic_reasoning: The documented failure is screw loosening due to insufficient preload retention under masticatory forces. Conical (Morse taper) connections provide superior mechanical anchoring compared to internal/external hex connections, as evidenced by higher removal forces (192.7 ± 10.9 N for conical vs. 174.3 ± 15.4 N for internal hex and 145.8 ± 12.6 N for external hex). This geometry inherently resists rotational and axial displacement, reducing reliance on screw preload alone. Additionally, Morse taper systems demonstrate diameter-independent mechanical stability and prosthetic-controlled failure patterns, unlike internal hex systems, which are sensitive to diameter reduction and bone loss.
candidates.expected_effect: The modification will reduce the incidence of screw loosening by improving the stability of the implant-abutment interface, thereby maintaining long-term preload under functional loads.
